According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple has reportedly been considering adding a feature to Apple Upgrade (Apple's trade-in programme) that would make setting up a new iPhone virtually seamless: Apple would copy your data to the new device in advance. However, the feature was never implemented.

The concept is simple: since users upgrade their devices on a regular monthly instalment plan, why not streamline the transfer process as much as possible? Here's Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reporting:

There are clearly several loopholes. First, your iCloud backup will inevitably be slightly out of date, since the data transfer can only happen when the new device is shipped, leaving a gap of several days — unless you opt for in-store pickup.

Privacy concerns are also a factor. If you already back up your data to iCloud, the fact that Apple holds your data should theoretically come as no surprise. But for the average user, there may be concerns about the process of transferring data to a new device, and whether anyone might窥探 the data along the way.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a new system in its stores called 'Presto' that allows staff to update an iPhone while it's still in the box. It's conceivable that this system could one day be expanded to support iCloud backup transfers, with no one ever needing to view your data.

Even so, the feature never made it to market — and that might actually be for the best.
